question: What is pharmacovigilance primarily concerned with?

options.C: Detecting and preventing adverse drug effects
options.D: Setting market prices for new medicines

explanation: Pharmacovigilance focuses on monitoring, assessing, and preventing harmful reactions linked to medication use in patients. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h1)

question: How does an adverse drug reaction differ from a predictable drug side effect?

options.A: It only happens when a patient overdoses intentionally
options.B: It is typically harmful and occurs at normal doses
options.C: It is always mild and requires no medical treatment
options.D: It has no relation to the pharmacological action

explanation: An adverse drug reaction is a noxious, unintended bodily response occurring at standard therapeutic doses. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which agency coordinates medication safety and post-market surveillance in Nigeria?
explanation: NAFDAC is the national body responsible for regulating and monitoring the safety of food and drugs in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why are clinical trials insufficient for discovering every possible drug reaction?

options.A: They involve small sample sizes before public release
options.B: Pharmaceutical companies refuse to document adverse events
options.C: Participants never take medications as prescribed
options.D: Researchers deliberately hide dangerous drug side effects

explanation: Clinical trials test drugs on limited groups of people, meaning rare reactions only show up after widespread public use. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the common color designation of the NAFDAC ADR reporting form?
explanation: The NAFDAC adverse drug reaction reporting tool is traditionally recognized and referred to as the Yellow Form. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of using a standardized reporting form nationwide?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for patient interviews
options.B: It allows easy comparison and analysis of collected data
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing medications
options.D: It forces doctors to prescribe only locally made drugs

explanation: A uniform format ensures that reports from different health facilities contain the same vital information for safe review. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which specific drug detail is essential on an ADR form to trace counterfeit or faulty batches?
explanation: Recording the batch number helps regulatory authorities trace specific production runs if a widespread safety issue arises. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why must traditional or herbal remedies be listed under concomitant medications?

options.A: To check for potential herb-drug interactions
options.C: To find out where the patient bought herbs
options.D: To calculate the total cost of patient care

explanation: Herbal products can interact with orthodox medicines and trigger unexpected adverse reactions in the body. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h4)

question: A patient develops a severe skin rash two days after starting a new antibiotic. What is your first documentation step on the ADR form?

options.A: Record the reaction details and the suspected antibiotic
options.B: Write a formal letter to the national newspaper
options.C: Contact the pharmaceutical manufacturing company abroad
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately from the hospital ward

explanation: Documenting the exact reaction and the offending drug forms the core foundation of any valid pharmacovigilance report. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is it necessary for the reporting nurse to include their professional contact details?

options.A: To allow regulatory officers to request clarification if needed
options.B: To update the patient's personal employment records
options.C: To ensure the nurse receives financial compensation for reporting
options.D: To prove that the hospital pharmacy has enough drug stock

explanation: Pharmacovigilance teams often need to follow up with the original reporter to gather missing clinical details. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h5)

question: What defines an adverse drug reaction as 'serious' in clinical reporting?

options.A: It results in death or prolongs hospitalization
options.B: It happens to patients over the age of sixty
options.C: It requires changing the drug brand name
options.D: It causes mild nausea for less than an hour

explanation: Serious adverse drug reactions involve life-threatening conditions, death, significant disability, or extended hospital stays. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a causality assessment on an ADR report?

options.A: To calculate the market price of the suspected drug
options.B: To determine if the drug actually caused the reaction
options.C: To check if the hospital pharmacy is running out of stock
options.D: To decide which nurse should care for the patient

explanation: Causality assessment evaluates the strength of the relationship between the medicine intake and the adverse event observed. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h6)

question: Where can completed paper ADR forms be submitted within Nigeria?

options.B: Local police stations for criminal investigation
options.C: NAFDAC zonal offices or designated committees

explanation: Completed reports are channeled through institutional drug committees or directly to NAFDAC zonal offices for processing. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h7)

question: What should a nurse do if new laboratory test results arrive after submitting an initial ADR report?

options.A: Throw away the old report and forget about the incident
options.B: Call the pharmaceutical manufacturer to demand a refund
options.C: Submit a follow-up report with the new clinical details
options.D: Wait until the patient is discharged to rewrite everything

explanation: Providing supplementary laboratory or outcome data ensures the safety database remains accurate and complete. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why does under-reporting of adverse drug reactions remain a major challenge in clinical settings?

options.A: NAFDAC strictly forbids nurses from filling out yellow forms
options.B: Patients refuse to take any medications prescribed in hospitals
options.C: Healthcare workers often assume others will report or neglect paperwork
options.D: Electronic computers have completely replaced paper documentation

explanation: Under-reporting frequently happens because busy clinicians assume a colleague has already filed the report or view it as extra work. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h8)

question: A patient complains of dizziness after taking a newly prescribed antihypertensive drug. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Prescribe a different medication to counteract the dizziness
options.B: Educate the patient, monitor vitals, and consider filing an ADR form
options.C: Tell the patient to stop all medications and never return to the clinic
options.D: Ignore the complaint because dizziness is completely normal

explanation: Nurses should assess the symptom, educate the patient, and document untoward drug reactions using proper reporting channels. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h8)
